jobs.title: Executive Director, Musizi University Foundation
jobs.description:
Executive Director, Musizi University Foundation

Location:
Remote (US-based preferred) with periodic international travel incl to Uganda.
Reports To:
Board of Directors, Musizi University Foundation
Status:
Full-time
Compensation:
$85,000/year

About Musizi University Foundation

Musizi University Foundation is the U.S.-based 501(c)(3) charitable organization established to support the growth and long-term sustainability of Musizi University in Uganda.
Musizi University is building a new model of higher education for Africa—one that combines the liberal arts, entrepreneurship, technology, and experiential learning to prepare graduates to solve Africa's greatest challenges with empathy, innovation, and integrity.
The Foundation exists to mobilize philanthropic investment, cultivate strategic partnerships, and engage a global community of supporters who believe in the transformative potential of higher education.

Position Summary

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive of Musizi University Foundation and is responsible for advancing the Foundation's mission through strategic leadership, fundraising, donor stewardship, organizational management, and external engagement.
Working closely with the Foundation Board and the leadership of Musizi University, the Executive Director will build the Foundation into a world-class philanthropic organization capable of attracting transformational investment from individuals, foundations, corporations, and institutional partners around the world.
This is an entrepreneurial leadership role suited for someone excited by building an organization from the ground up and helping shape one of Africa's most innovative universities.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Lead the strategic growth of Musizi University Foundation.
Develop and implement multi-year fundraising and organizational strategies.
Work closely with the Foundation Board to establish priorities, annual goals, and performance metrics.
Serve as a key strategic advisor to Musizi University's leadership.
Help position Musizi as a leading philanthropic investment opportunity in African higher education.

Fundraising and Development

Develop and execute comprehensive annual and long-term fundraising plans.
Build and manage a pipeline of major donors and prospective supporters.
Cultivate relationships with philanthropists, family foundations, corporations, and institutional funders.
Lead major gift solicitation and stewardship efforts.
Prepare and oversee grant proposals and funding applications.
Design donor recognition and stewardship programs.
Support capital campaigns for scholarships, campus development, and strategic initiatives.

Board Relations

Partner with the Foundation Board to strengthen governance and fundraising engagement.
Support Board recruitment and orientation.
Prepare Board materials, reports, and strategic updates.
Facilitate Board meetings and committee work.

Partnerships and External Relations

Represent Musizi University Foundation with donors, partners, universities, corporations, and government agencies.
Develop strategic partnerships that advance the University's mission.
Build relationships with alumni, diaspora communities, and global networks interested in African higher education.
Serve as a compelling ambassador for Musizi's vision.

Organizational Leadership

Build and supervise the Foundation team over time.
Establish operational systems, policies, and administrative processes.
Oversee Foundation finances in partnership with the Treasurer and Board.
Ensure legal and regulatory compliance for a U.S. nonprofit organization.
Manage external consultants and service providers.

Communications

Help shape the Foundation's fundraising communications strategy.
Develop compelling cases for support.
Oversee donor communications, newsletters, annual reports, and campaign materials.
Collaborate with the University's communications team to ensure consistent messaging.

Qualifications

Required
Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.
Seven or more years of progressively responsible leadership experience in nonprofit management, fundraising, philanthropy, higher education, or a related field.
Demonstrated success securing major gifts and managing donor relationships.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong strategic planning and organizational leadership abilities.
Experience working with boards of directors.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced entrepreneurial environment.
Willingness to travel internationally.

Preferred
Experience launching or scaling nonprofit organizations.
Experience in higher education fundraising or university advancement.
Familiarity with African education or international development.
Experience managing grants from foundations and institutional donors.
Existing relationships within philanthropic, corporate, or higher education networks.
Experience leading capital or comprehensive fundraising campaigns.

Desired Competencies

Strategic Agility
Business Acumen
Composure
Decision Quality
Leadership
Entrepreneurial mindset
Strategic thinker
Relationship builder
Exceptional storyteller
Strong project manager
High integrity and sound judgment
Cultural humility and global perspective
Results-oriented with strong execution skills
Collaborative leadership style
Passion for educational transformation

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

The Executive Director will be evaluated annually based on progress across the following areas.
1. Fundraising & Revenue Growth

Raise annual philanthropic revenue in line with Board-approved targets.
Secure 10–20 new ultra major donor ($10,000 or above) prospects annually.
Submit 10–15 high-quality grant proposals annually.
Achieve a year-over-year increase in unrestricted funding.
Diversify funding sources across individuals, foundations, corporations, and institutional grants.
Maintain a healthy fundraising pipeline with qualified prospects at each stage of cultivation.

2. Donor Engagement & Stewardship

Maintain regular, meaningful engagement with existing donors.
Ensure timely stewardship, recognition, and impact reporting.
Develop personalized engagement strategies for major donors.
Increase donor retention and recurring giving.

KPIs

Donor retention rate of 75% or higher.
100% of major donors receive at least two meaningful stewardship interactions annually.
All donor reports delivered on schedule.
Increase recurring donors each year.

3. Strategic Partnerships

Develop partnerships that strengthen Musizi University's academic excellence, student opportunities, and financial sustainability.
Expand relationships with corporations, family foundations, and philanthropic organizations.

KPIs

Establish 5–10 new strategic partnerships annually.
Secure corporate sponsorships and foundation collaborations aligned with Musizi's priorities.
Increase the number of collaborative initiatives supporting scholarships, research, internships, or innovation.

4. Organizational Development

Build strong operational systems for the Foundation.
Strengthen governance and Board engagement.
Ensure legal, financial, and regulatory compliance.

KPIs

Annual operating plan approved and implemented.
Annual budget achieved within agreed variance.
Successful completion of required nonprofit filings and compliance obligations.
Positive Board evaluation of Executive Director performance.
Recruit and onboard additional Foundation staff as growth requires.

5. Communications & Visibility

Increase awareness of Musizi University among philanthropic audiences.
Position the Foundation as a trusted investment partner for transformational education in Africa.

KPIs

Publish an annual impact report.
Deliver quarterly donor communications.
Increase Foundation visibility through speaking engagements, conferences, and strategic events.
Grow engagement across newsletters, donor events, and digital communications.

6. Collaboration with Musizi University

Maintain strong alignment between Foundation activities and University priorities.
Support fundraising for strategic institutional initiatives, including scholarships, academic programs, faculty development, and campus expansion.

KPIs

Quarterly strategic planning meetings with University leadership.
Timely reporting on fundraising progress and donor commitments.
Successful execution of fundraising campaigns supporting University priorities.
High levels of satisfaction from University leadership regarding Foundation partnership and responsiveness.

Overall Measures of Success

Success in this role will be demonstrated by the Executive Director's ability to:
Build a sustainable culture of philanthropy around Musizi University.
Grow annual philanthropic support while strengthening long-term donor relationships.
Position Musizi University Foundation as a respected and trusted philanthropic organization.
Expand the University's network of strategic partners and supporters globally.
Build the organizational systems, team, and governance structures necessary to support the Foundation's long-term growth and impact.

Why Join Musizi?

This is an opportunity to help build one of Africa's most ambitious higher education institutions from the ground up.
Rather than joining an established organization, you will help create one—working alongside visionary educators, entrepreneurs, and global partners to expand access to transformative education and prepare a new generation of African leaders.
Your work will directly contribute to scholarships, academic excellence, campus development, research, and the long-term sustainability of an institution designed to serve Africa for generations to come.

Job Description

The Development Program Director is a high-visibility leadership role within the Program Management Office (PMO) at Honeywell Aerospace Defense Systems Division located in San Diego, CA site. This position, reporting to the Sr. Director of Program Management, will lead a team of Program Managers responsible for a portfolio of Radio Frequency (RF) electronic components development, iR&D, and production programs for land, air, sea, and space applications. These include design to specifications, development of commercial products, and transition to production (NPI) of roughly $100M. The Development Program Director is expected to actively cultivate strong relationships with key development customers, positioning Honeywell Aerospace to win large-scale production programs.

Responsibilities

New Business Proposals & Development Program Initiation:

Partner with BD and proposal management leadership to ensure new business proposals are effectively lead, and orchestrated to achieve timely review, approval, and submission to customers.
Ensure development program manager team conducts thorough reviews of Basis of Estimates (BOEs) for labor, materials, and other program support functions, ensuring the proposals are executable and align with program goals.
Cultivate strong relationships with existing and potential customers, ensuring that proposals align with their needs and long-term strategic goals.
Support proposal negotiations with internal contracts staff and customers, maintaining close engagement with customer representatives to secure favorable terms and alignment on expectations.
Identify follow-on business and growth opportunities through development work that can evolve into larger production contracts.

Program Execution & Development

Drive program management accountability to create and take ownership of program plans, budget management, technical oversight, financial, and scheduling aspects of development programs.
Manage funds and reallocate resources as needed, ensuring that programs meet financial targets and scope.
Regularly monitor orders, revenue, profit, and cash flow, ensuring alignment with both short-term and long-term program objectives.
Drive risk and opportunity management throughout the program lifecycle, identifying and mitigating risks while capitalizing on opportunities.
Ensure consistent communication and collaboration across the Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), with Program Managers driving weekly meetings to track program progress, resolve issues, and close actions in a timely manner.
Ensure compliance with all applicable government, company, customer, and industry specifications and regulations (e.g., FAR, DFAR, ITAR).
Champion contractual integrity, ensuring that all contracts are adhered to, including compliance with legal and regulatory requirements in proposal submissions and contract execution.
Establish and maintain strategic business relationships with key customers to position Honeywell Aerospace as a trusted partner for long-term development and production contracts.

Customer & Stakeholder Communication

Be the visible, active, engaged and recognized leader of the Development Program Management team
Build and maintain strong customer relationships that complement customer relationships of your Program Management team.
Provide regular status updates and reports to leadership, functional departments, and customers, ensuring alignment and transparency on health and progress of your portfolio programs.
Identify opportunities to expand customer portfolios, collaborating with business development teams to develop strategies for growing existing accounts and winning new, large production contracts.

Product Management

Lead Commercial Product Management for the Defense Systems organization.
Individually, and through subordinate product managers as required, create, communicate, sell and manage Research and Development (R&D), customer interaction, and product build plans to new commercial RF products.
Support Business Development in plans to sell commercial products to customers.

Functional Leadership

Define and insist on program management excellence from your team to achieve near flawless development program execution.
Work collaboratively with Engineering leadership to mature program and engineering management. processes that properly propose and execute engineering development on schedule and within budgets.
Ensure your Program Management staff has the necessary tools and training to ensure their success.
Regularly conduct meetings with direct reports to mentor, coach, develop, and assess talent to establish career development plans.

Qualifications

MUST HAVE:

Thirteen (13) years of experience in program management, ideally in the electronics/communications sector supporting U.S. DOD or foreign military governments.
Ten (10) years of leadership and people management experience.
Experience managing new development programs with a cross-functional team, demonstrating strong leadership and collaboration across technical, financial, and operational functions.
Experience managing complex programs with >$10M in annual revenue
Demonstrated ability to manage A&D P&L including achieving monthly, quarterly, yearly targets for orders, revenue, gross margin, and cash
Experience leading and developing multiple direct reporting Program Managers
Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

Us Person Requirements

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent

We Value

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Technology, Math, Science or Business Administration.
Master’s Degree
PMP Certification or similar project management qualifications.
Experience in the Aerospace and Defense industries, particularly with electronic hardware development programs, RF/Microwave Products, or manufacturing electronic products.
Experience managing complex development programs or serving in a deputy capacity for large, high-risk programs.
Strong background in new business development, particularly in growing customer portfolios and winning large production contracts.
Background in management of commercial product development and market introduction.

Job Summary:
The Director of Communications provides strategic leadership and oversight for churchwide communications, marketing, branding, and creative strategy at Cottonwood Creek Church. This position is responsible for ensuring church communication is clear, consistent, effective, and aligned with the mission and ministry priorities of the church. The Director works closely with pastors, senior leadership, ministry leaders, and staff to develop communication strategies, guide creative direction, strengthen and protect the Cottonwood Creek Church brand, and move projects from concept through execution.

Essential Functions

Lead the overall communications and marketing strategy for Cottonwood Creek Church.
Serve as the primary steward of the Cottonwood Creek Church brand.
Develop communication plans for sermon series, major events, seasonal campaigns, ministries, and churchwide initiatives.
Oversee messaging across web, email, text, social media, print, signage, video, advertising, and other communication channels.
Provide creative direction for graphic design, photography, video, environmental graphics, and promotional campaigns.
Partner with pastors, senior leadership, and ministry leaders to understand ministry priorities and develop communication plans, messaging, audiences, timelines, and calls to action that support the mission and ministry of Cottonwood Creek Church.
Exercise sound judgment and discretion regarding sensitive, confidential, or time-sensitive church communications, working with Senior Leadership as appropriate before information is released internally or publicly.
Lead and develop Communications Department staff, contractors, interns, and volunteers.
Oversee the church website and digital communication strategy.
Manage communication calendars, project priorities, workflows, deadlines, and production schedules.
Oversee outside vendors, printers, agencies, and creative partners as needed.
Maintain brand standards and ensure consistent use of church and ministry identities.
Provide oversight for churchwide signage, promotional materials, branded apparel, and environmental communication.
Evaluate communication effectiveness and identify opportunities to improve reach, engagement, and clarity.

Job Requirements And Personal Qualifications

Education:
Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, public relations, advertising, journalism, design, or a related field preferred.

Job Skills:
Strong strategic communication, writing, editing, proofreading, and presentation skills; strong understanding of branding, marketing, digital communications, social media, websites, email marketing, and audience engagement; ability to provide creative direction across multiple mediums; excellent organizational and project-management skills; ability to manage multiple priorities, projects, deadlines, vendors, budgets, and production schedules; strong leadership and team-development skills; ability to communicate effectively and professionally with pastors, senior leadership, ministry leaders, staff, vendors, volunteers, and church members; collaborative while able to make clear decisions and provide direction; proactive, discerning, dependable, flexible, and detail-oriented; able to anticipate communication needs and build effective systems and processes; exercises sound judgment and a high degree of discretion and confidentiality.

Personal Qualifications:
Have a personal relationship with Jesus Christ with consistent evidence of fruit in your personal life; demonstrate spiritual maturity and a servant’s heart; motivated to serve God and support the mission, beliefs, leadership, and ministry philosophy of Cottonwood Creek Church; understand that church communication is about more than promoting events and should ultimately help people encounter the Gospel, find biblical community, and take meaningful next steps in their faith; ability to lead with humility, wisdom, creativity, and excellence; consistently use good judgment and demonstrate a strong willingness to do what is necessary for the safety and betterment of the church spiritually, ethically, financially, and organizationally. Membership at Cottonwood Creek Church is required.

Other Information

Professional experience in communications, marketing, branding, creative services, or a related field.
Leadership or team-management experience preferred.
Experience developing integrated communication or marketing campaigns.
Experience managing vendors, budgets, timelines, and production processes.
Church, ministry, nonprofit, or mission-driven communications experience is a plus.
Due to the nature of church communications, occasional evening, weekend, Sunday, and special-event availability may be required.

jobs.description:
Executive Director
Pier 360
Job Location: Vancouver, Washington (On-Site)
Compensation: $130,000–$150,000 annually
Motus Recruiting and Staffing is proud to partner with Pier 360 in its search for its next Executive Director.
ABOUT PIER 360
Founded in 1995 as Consumer Voices Are Born (CVAB), Pier 360 is a peer-led nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering individuals and families through mental health and substance use recovery. Guided by its mission to use peer support to share hope, empower renewal, and support recovery, the organization believes that recovery is possible for everyone. Rooted in lived experience, Pier 360 fosters a recovery-centered culture where peers walk alongside others on their journey toward hope, healing, and independence.
Today, Pier 360 employs approximately 40 team members and operates four facilities serving Southwest Washington. Through its Peer Academy, peer support services, recovery housing, and wellness programs, the organization delivers innovative, person-centered services that strengthen resilience, expand access to recovery resources, and improve the health and well-being of the communities it serves. Strong partnerships with healthcare providers, community organizations, and public agencies further amplify its impact across the region.
Pier 360 is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and welcoming environment where every individual is treated with dignity, respect, and compassion. The organization recognizes that lived experience strengthens its workforce, informs its services, and advances its mission.
To learn more about Pier 360, visit their website: https://www.pier360.org/
OVERVIEW OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR POSITION

Reports To: Board of Directors
Direct Reports: CFO, HR Director, Business Services Director, Program/Platform Development, Data Team, Administrative Leadership
Collaborates With: Board of Directors, behavioral health partners, county and state agencies, healthcare systems, funders, community organizations, advocacy groups, and legislative stakeholders.
The Executive Director provides visionary leadership for Pier 360, guiding the organization's mission to empower individuals through peer-led mental health and substance use recovery services. Reporting to the Board of Directors, this leader will foster a culture rooted in recovery, lived experience, innovation, and collaboration while overseeing strategic planning, organizational operations, financial sustainability, and community partnerships. As the organization's chief ambassador, the Executive Director will ensure Pier 360 continues to grow its impact while remaining grounded in its Core Values and commitment to peer support. This leader works across all bureaus and offices to operationalize equity in governance, budgeting, workforce practices, community engagement, and service outcomes. The Executive Director will embody and champion Pier 360’s Core Values of Respect, Responsibility, Empowerment, Genuineness, Welcoming, Innovation, Justice, and Curiosity, ensuring they guide leadership, decision-making, workplace culture, and service delivery.
ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
Executive Leadership & Organizational Strategy
Provide visionary leadership that advances Pier 360's mission, Core Focus, strategic priorities, and peer-led philosophy while ensuring long-term organizational sustainability.
Provide executive oversight of organizational operations, talent, leadership development, and performance while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and recovery-oriented culture grounded in the organization's Core Values.
Lead strategic planning, organizational change, innovation, and continuous improvement by identifying opportunities that strengthen infrastructure, operational excellence, and long-term impact.
Serve as the organization's chief ambassador, championing behavioral health, recovery, peer support, and community partnerships throughout Southwest Washington.

Financial Stewardship & Resource Development
Provide executive oversight of the organization's approximately $3 million budget while partnering with the Chief Financial Officer to ensure long-term financial sustainability.
Lead fundraising, grant development, donor cultivation, and diversified revenue strategies that strengthen organizational growth and community impact.
Oversee contracts, compliance, risk management, vendor relationships, and organizational reporting while ensuring responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
Guide communications, marketing, and development initiatives that increase visibility, strengthen partnerships, and expand funding opportunities.

Program Leadership & Operational Excellence
Champion recovery-oriented, peer-led behavioral health services while ensuring programs remain aligned with Pier 360's mission, Core Focus, and Core Values.
Ensure compliance with behavioral health licensing, regulatory requirements, contracts, and quality standards while promoting evidence-informed practices.
Lead program development, innovation, continuous improvement, and evaluation to strengthen organizational outcomes and community impact.
Support excellence across peer support, mental health recovery, substance use recovery, recovery housing, and Peer Academy programming.

Board Governance & Organizational Stewardship
Partner closely with the Board of Directors by serving as its chief executive advisor and Board Secretary while supporting governance, strategic planning, and organizational accountability.
Maintain productive relationships with Board leadership, legal counsel, and key stakeholders while serving as the organization's authorized representative for contracts and legal agreements.
Provide transparent communication, strategic recommendations, and organizational reporting that support informed Board decision-making.
Assist the Board with policy development, succession planning, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Community Engagement & Advocacy
Serve as Pier 360's primary ambassador by cultivating strong relationships with healthcare providers, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, funders, legislators, and community partners.
Advocate for policies and initiatives that strengthen behavioral health, recovery services, and peer support at the local, regional, and state levels.
Build strategic partnerships that expand organizational visibility, community impact, and long-term sustainability.
Represent Pier 360 in collaborative initiatives while monitoring legislative and public policy developments affecting behavioral health and recovery.

Organizational Culture & Leadership Development
Foster an inclusive, supportive, and psychologically safe workplace grounded in Pier 360's Core Values, recovery philosophy, and commitment to peer-led services.
Coach, mentor, and develop leaders while strengthening succession planning, employee engagement, and cross-functional collaboration.
Build trust through transparency, authenticity, humility, and emotional intelligence while supporting professional growth for employees with lived experience.
Cultivate a workplace where employees feel respected, empowered, connected, and inspired to advance Pier 360's mission.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum
5+ years of Executive leadership experience within nonprofit, behavioral health, healthcare, human services, recovery, or related organizations.
Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and executive leadership experience.
Demonstrated experience leading organizational strategy, operations, and change management.
Experience overseeing budgets, contracts, grants, fundraising initiatives, and financial stewardship.
Experience partnering with nonprofit Boards of Directors and supporting effective governance.
Experience supervising and developing multidisciplinary leadership teams.
Demonstrated ability to build strategic partnerships and effectively represent an organization publicly.
Strong communication, relationship-building, and organizational leadership skills.

Preferred
Lived experience with recovery, behavioral health, or substance use recovery.
Experience working within peer support or peer-led organizations.
Licensed Behavioral Health Agency leadership experience.
Knowledge of Medicaid-funded services, behavioral health systems, and regulatory compliance.
Experience leading grant-funded and contract-funded organizations.
Demonstrated fundraising, grant development, and donor cultivation experience.
Experience leading organizational growth, infrastructure development, and strategic planning.
Political acumen with experience working alongside government agencies, healthcare systems, and community partners.
Experience developing healthy workplace cultures while coaching and mentoring future leaders.

Lead through humility, authenticity, and emotional intelligence.
Understand and value lived experience as a foundational element of recovery.
Build leadership capacity across the organization while developing future leaders.
Foster collaboration while reducing organizational silos.
Balance strategic vision with operational excellence and strong execution.
Champion innovation while preserving Pier 360's mission, culture, and peer-led philosophy.
Build sustainable funding strategies and strengthen community partnerships.
Lead with transparency, accountability, curiosity, and compassion.

Supervises:

Strategic & Executive Leadership

Racial Equity & Social Justice

UGA is currently ranked among the top 20 public universities in U.S. News & World Report. Franklin College of Arts and Sciences

The Franklin College of Arts and Sciences is the oldest, largest, and most academically diverse college at the University of Georgia. In many ways, it is at the heart of UGA, the nation’s first state-chartered institution of higher education. The first classes were taught in 1801 in a forest clearing on what is now the University’s historic North Campus. In 1806, the first permanent brick building was constructed on campus and named Franklin College in honor of Benjamin Franklin. The building, which was later renamed Old College, is the oldest structure in Athens and houses the administrative offices of the Franklin College of Arts and Sciences as well as classroom space. Franklin College and University of Georgia were often used interchangeably to describe the fledgling institution until 1859, when the College of Law became the second college on a campus that now boasts 16 schools and colleges. The Franklin College of Arts and Sciences is the largest and most academically diverse college at the University of Georgia with over 11,000 students, over 800 faculty and three of the five most popular undergraduate majors at UGA – biology, psychology, and computer science. The college has 78 undergraduate majors, 35 master’s degree programs and 31 doctoral degree programs. The Franklin College of Arts and Sciences is the oldest, largest, and most academically diverse college at the University of Georgia. The first classes were taught in 1801 in a forest clearing on what is now the University’s historic North Campus. The building, which was later renamed Old College, is the oldest structure in Athens and houses the administrative offices of the Franklin College of Arts and Sciences as well as classroom space. Franklin College and University of Georgia were often used interchangeably to describe the fledgling institution until 1859, when the College of Law became the second college on a campus that now boasts 16 schools and colleges. At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.

Job Description

Parsons is seeking an experienced Program Director
to lead and expand major water and wastewater programs throughout the State of Texas. Based in Houston, this executive-level role will be responsible for program strategy, client relationship management, delivery oversight, construction management, team leadership, and business development.

The successful candidate will have extensive experience delivering complex water and wastewater infrastructure programs, managing multidisciplinary teams, overseeing construction and program controls, and developing trusted relationships with public-sector and private-sector clients. This position requires a strategic leader who can balance technical delivery, operational excellence, financial performance, and long-term client growth.

Key Responsibilities

Construction Management

Provide oversight of construction management activities for water and wastewater treatment plants, collection and distribution systems, pipelines, pump stations, reservoirs, lift stations, storage facilities, and related infrastructure.
Review contractor performance, construction schedules, payment applications, change orders, claims, safety performance, and quality compliance.
Support constructability reviews, procurement strategies, bid evaluations, and contract negotiations.
Manage construction risks and facilitate timely resolution of field, contractual, and technical issues.
Promote a strong safety culture and ensure that construction activities align with project safety plans and corporate standards.
Support the development and implementation of alternative delivery methods, including design-bid-build, design-build, construction manager at risk, progressive design-build, and public-private partnership approaches where appropriate.

Program Delivery

Provide executive leadership for large, complex water and wastewater programs across Texas.
Establish program vision, goals, governance structures, delivery strategies, and performance objectives.
Direct the planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and closeout of infrastructure programs.
Ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contractual, regulatory, and quality requirements.
Lead program controls, including scope, schedule, cost, risk, change management, quality, and document control.
Oversee the coordination of engineering, construction management, program management, environmental, permitting, procurement, and commissioning teams.
Identify and resolve project and program-level issues before they affect cost, schedule, quality, or client satisfaction.
Implement best practices, standardized processes, and performance metrics across the program portfolio.
Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including environmental, utility, procurement, and construction requirements.

Client and Stakeholder Relationships

Serve as the senior point of contact for key clients, including municipalities, water authorities, regional agencies, utilities, industrial clients, and other public-sector entities.
Build and maintain trusted, long-term relationships with client executives, elected officials, board members, regulators, contractors, consultants, and community stakeholders.
Lead executive-level client meetings, program reviews, strategic planning sessions, and issue-resolution discussions.
Anticipate client needs and proactively identify opportunities to improve program outcomes.
Develop communications strategies that clearly convey program status, risks, financial performance, accomplishments, and upcoming priorities.
Represent Parsons at industry events, professional associations, community meetings, and client-facing forums throughout Texas.

Business Development and Growth

Develop and execute strategic growth plans for water and wastewater services across Texas.
Identify, qualify, and pursue new program management, engineering, construction management, and infrastructure opportunities.
Lead client account planning and maintain an active pipeline of potential pursuits.
Develop capture strategies, pursuit plans, teaming arrangements, and win strategies.
Participate in proposal development, including technical approaches, staffing plans, project understanding, pricing strategies, presentations, and interviews.
Establish and maintain relationships with owners, utilities, engineering firms, contractors, and industry partners.
Monitor market trends, capital improvement programs, funding opportunities, regulatory developments, and infrastructure investment priorities.
Position Parsons for long-term program and project opportunities through differentiated technical, management, and delivery solutions.

Team and Operational Leadership

Recruit, mentor, and lead high-performing program and project teams.
Establish clear expectations for accountability, collaboration, communication, and professional development.
Coordinate with regional, national, and corporate leadership to align resources and business objectives.
Manage staffing plans, utilization, financial performance, and resource requirements across the program.
Foster an inclusive work environment that values safety, integrity, innovation, teamwork, and client service.
Support succession planning and development of future program and project leaders.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
Typically 20+ progressive experience in water/wastewater infrastructure, program management, construction management, engineering delivery, or a related field.
Significant experience leading major water and wastewater programs, preferably for municipal, regional, state, industrial, or utility clients.
Demonstrated experience with the delivery of complex capital improvement programs involving multiple projects, stakeholders, funding sources, and delivery methods.
Extensive construction management experience, including contractor oversight, contract administration, schedule management, cost control, claims, change management, and quality assurance.
Proven success managing senior-level client relationships and serving as a trusted advisor to executive stakeholders.
Demonstrated business development and capture experience, including leading pursuits, developing proposals, and securing new work.
Strong understanding of water and wastewater treatment facilities, conveyance systems, pump stations, pipelines, storage, resiliency, and related infrastructure.
Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and geographically dispersed project personnel.
Strong financial management skills, including budget development, forecasting, earned value, profitability, and performance reporting.
Excellent written, verbal, presentation, negotiation, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to travel throughout Texas and occasionally to other locations as business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Engineer license, preferably in Texas.
Project Management Professional certification.
Design-Build Institute of America certification or comparable alternative delivery experience.
Certified Construction Manager certification.
Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field.
Experience with Texas municipalities, regional water authorities, utility districts, state agencies, or other public-sector clients.
Familiarity with Texas regulatory and permitting requirements related to water and wastewater infrastructure.
Experience with major program funding mechanisms, including state revolving funds, federal infrastructure programs, grants, bonds, and public financing.
Experience delivering programs using alternative delivery methods such as design-build, CMAR, progressive design-build, or public-private partnerships.
Established professional network within the Texas water, wastewater, infrastructure, and construction markets.

Core Competencies

The Ideal Candidate Will Demonstrate

Strategic leadership: Ability to set direction and translate organizational goals into successful program outcomes.
Client service orientation: Commitment to developing trusted, long-term client partnerships.
Business acumen: Ability to manage program performance while identifying opportunities for growth.
Construction expertise: Strong understanding of field execution, contractor management, and delivery risk.
Communication: Ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, executives, public officials, and community stakeholders.
Collaboration: Ability to lead across disciplines, organizations, and delivery partners.
Accountability: Consistent focus on safety, quality, ethics, financial performance, and commitments.
Adaptability: Ability to manage changing priorities, complex issues, and high-visibility programs.
Integrity: Demonstrated commitment to ethical conduct, transparency, and professional standards.

Work Environment

This position will be based in Houston, Texas
, with responsibility for programs and client relationships throughout the State of Texas. The role will include a combination of office, field, and client-site work, as well as regular travel to project locations, meetings, presentations, and industry events.

Why Join Parsons

At Parsons, you will have the opportunity to lead transformational water and wastewater infrastructure programs that support resilient, sustainable, and thriving communities across Texas. This role offers the ability to influence major infrastructure investments, work with prominent public and private clients, lead talented technical professionals, and contribute to the growth of a nationally recognized engineering and infrastructure organization.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Parsons is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants and employees. Employment decisions are made without regard to legally protected characteristics and are based on qualifications, performance, business needs, and organizational requirements.

None
